| [CASE-165](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-165.md) v3 | A dynamic beta–Bernoulli latent-feature model of an organization's members: a finite Indian buffet prior over who holds which interpretive features, a sticky logistic transition for holding them, activations, and team, communication and authorization layers above; at the proposed size of sixteen features it falls well short of the Indian buffet process it quotes, its persistence term does not hold rare features, and the difference between having a capacity and using it is not identified from the outputs | The owner's T22 ("maybe we could benefit from a restaurant process model, like an indian buffet model"), developed at T23 ("flesh out our proposed generating probability model further") into a full generative specification for the Northstar firm, and carried to transformer training at T24. Its facts are its definition, and four of them are not what T23 says: at K = 16 the prior expects 6.83 features, not αH₁₂ = 9.31; a held rare feature is kept with probability 0.16 a day; and having, using and splitting features are confounded in the reconstruction. It shows what such a model would have to get right before its features could count for anything. | Proposed |
